pageTitle: Lesson 10 · Rainy Days and Long Queues
eyebrow: Lesson 10 · B1 · Good Manners in Public · 20 câu
heading: Rainy Days and Long Queues
source: Bài đọc phỏng theo Good Manners in Public – Ann Ingalls (The Child's World, 2013), tr. 8–9, 12–13.
credit: Tranh minh hoạ: Ronnie Rooney, trong Good Manners in Public (The Child's World, 2013). Dùng cho mục đích học tập.

paras.label: A
paras.text: On rainy days, umbrellas are everywhere, and they come with their own manners. If you are sharing an umbrella, let the taller person hold it. When you meet someone else with an umbrella on a {narrow|narrow} path, lift yours higher if you can so that they can pass {underneath|underneath}. Just be careful not to knock them on the head!

paras.label: B
paras.text: Open your umbrella after you get off a bus or train, not inside, and shake it before you get back on. Never put a wet umbrella on an empty seat: nobody wants to sit down on a {soggy|soggy} seat. In Japan, people leave wet umbrellas at the door; many shops and restaurants have special umbrella {stands|stands}, and bringing a {dripping|dripping} umbrella inside is seen as rude.

paras.label: C
paras.text: Queues are another part of daily life. We {queue|queue} to pay in shops and to get lunch at school. If you are not sure where the line starts, watch other people and stand behind them. Never push to the front or {cut in|cut in}, which could even knock someone's food off their tray.

paras.label: D
paras.text: In England, cutting in line is called "{queue jumping|queue jumping}", and English people consider it extremely rude. Wherever you are, give the person in front of you a little space. It is no fun to have someone {breathing down your neck|breathing down your neck}!

paras.label: E
paras.text: Most importantly, be {patient|patient}. The line will move, and you will reach the front soon enough.

parts.title: Part 1 · Which paragraph?
parts.instr: Đoạn nào (A–E) chứa thông tin dưới đây?

items.label: A paragraph that explains how to share an umbrella
items.why: Đoạn A: *let the taller person hold it.*

items.label: A paragraph about umbrellas and public transport
items.why: Đoạn B: mở ô sau khi xuống xe buýt, tàu.

items.label: A paragraph that tells you what to do if you don't know where a line begins
items.why: Đoạn C: *watch other people and stand behind them.*

items.label: A paragraph that gives a name for pushing in front of others
A paragraph that reminds you the wait will not last forever
items.why: Đoạn E: *you will reach the front soon enough.*

parts.title: Part 2 · Reading comprehension
parts.instr: Chọn đáp án đúng hoặc True / False.

questions.q: Who should hold an umbrella that two people are sharing?
The writer suggests opening your umbrella before you get off the bus.
questions.why: Sai. *Open your umbrella after you get off.*

questions.q: What do many shops and restaurants in Japan provide?
options: stands for wet umbrellas by the door
questions.why: *many shops and restaurants have special umbrella stands.*

questions.q: According to paragraph C, what could happen if you cut in?
options: You could knock someone's food off their tray.
You could get your lunch for free.
questions.why: *…which could even knock someone's food off their tray.*

questions.q: English people think queue jumping is very rude.
What is the main idea of the whole text?
options: Everyday situations need patience and thought for others.
Umbrellas are more useful in Japan.
English people are the politest in the world.
questions.why: Cả bài nói về cách nghĩ cho người khác khi trời mưa và khi xếp hàng.

parts.title: Part 3 · Picture tasks
parts.instr: Quan sát tranh minh hoạ trong sách và trả lời.

questions.q: What mistake can you see in the picture?
options: A wet umbrella has been left on a seat.
Someone is opening an umbrella outside.
The woman is cutting in line.
questions.why: Ô ướt để trên ghế – điều đoạn B khuyên không nên làm.
questions.alt: An older woman with a handbag stands near a bus seat where a wet red umbrella has been left; a boy sits beside it

questions.q: If the woman sits on that seat, what will it be like?
questions.alt: An older woman with a handbag stands near a bus seat where a wet red umbrella has been left; a boy sits beside it

questions.q: Which advice from paragraph D would help the children in this picture?
options: Give the person in front of you a little space.
Leave the line and come back later.
questions.why: Các bạn đứng quá sát nhau → *give the person in front of you a little space.*
questions.alt: Children standing very close together in a line

parts.title: Part 4 · Gapped text
parts.instr: Đọc đoạn văn ngắn và chọn câu phù hợp cho mỗi chỗ trống. Có 2 câu thừa.
parts.text: It was raining heavily when we got to the bus stop. [1] When the bus arrived, a long queue had formed. [2] As I sat down, I realised I had made one mistake. [3]
options: My little brother and I shared one umbrella, and I held it because I'm taller.
We waited patiently and got on after the people in front of us.
I had put my dripping umbrella on the seat next to me, and a lady was about to sit on it.
We pushed to the front so that we could get the best seats.
The sun was shining brightly, so we didn't need an umbrella.

items.why: Trời mưa → hai anh em che chung ô.
Có hàng dài → kiên nhẫn chờ. Câu *pushed to the front* không phù hợp vì sau đó chỉ nhắc *one mistake*.
*One mistake* = để ô ướt trên ghế.

parts.title: Part 5 · Words in context
parts.instr: Đoán nghĩa của từ/cụm từ dựa vào ngữ cảnh.

questions.q: *…nobody wants to sit down on a soggy seat* (B). **Soggy** means…
*Never push to the front or cut in* (C). To **cut in** is to…
options: go in front of people who were already waiting

questions.q: *…someone breathing down your neck!* (D). This means someone is…
questions.why: Đứng sát đến mức thở vào gáy → quá gần.
